newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Honeywell eyes new markets with Measurex.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Honeywell eyes new markets with Measurex.

text.p: Honeywell Inc sees its pending $600 million acquisition of Measurex Corp as a gateway into new markets and potentially stronger growth, said chief financial officer William Hjerpe.
"We're expecting both top-line and bottom-line synergies from the transaction," Hjerpe told Reuters in a telephone interview on Monday.
The transaction, expected to be completed by early March, "is seen as neutral to earnings in 1997 but accretive in 1998 and beyond," Hjerpe said.

Measurex, a large provider of paper machine integrated control systems, "is very strong in stable markets like North America and Europe and also in emerging markets in Asia, Latin America. It has a strong market share in Japan," he said.
Hjerpe described the overlap in the two companies' businesses as "insignificant."
"This transaction will combine Honeywell's strength on the pulping (distributed controls) side with Measurex's strength on the paper machine (process controls) side," Hjerpe said.
He added, "Through the combination, we'll have a pulp and paper business that exceeds $500 million," Hjerpe said.
In 1996, the pulp and paper segment accounted for about $200 million of Honeywell's revenues, which totaled $7.31 billion for the year.
Minneapolis-based Honeywell has a similar profile as Measurex in that both companies ship about 50 percent of their control system products to offshore customers.

In addition, Measurex, a Cupertino, Calif.-based control systems manufacturer, is involved in non-paper businesses new to Honeywell, particularly plastics, steel and non-ferrous metals. Measurex posted 1996 earnings of $2.25 a share on revenues of $416 million.
"We have reviewed the transaction with the credit rating agencies, and they found it is a good strategic fit and well within the bounds of our existing credit rating," Hjerpe said.
"The additional debt will not cause any kind of (negative) impact on the company's credit worthiness," said Hjerpe.
Analysts approved of the deal as well. Natwest Securities analyst Jonas Stiklorius said, "It's a great fit, combining the strengths of both businesses."
Measurex will be run within Honeywell's industrial automation and control unit by John Gingerich, Measurex president. Hjerpe said it will remain based in California.

Hjerpe said some of Measurex' 2,800 employees would lose their jobs once that company was no longer public, but he would not specify how many. Measurex chairman and chief executive officer David Bossen will stay on in an advisory capacity for an unspecified period.
Of the transaction, Hjerpe said, "We've established an objective between Honeywell and Measurex to reduce our combined cost base by five percent in the first year. It would grow from there."
On the news, Measurex' stock rose 10-1/4 to 34-1/2. Honeywell as off 1/2 at 69-1/2.
